findings.title: Strict encode emits a 77-character line (exceeds RFC 76-char limit) before the final soft break
findings.property: in strict mode (full RFC 1521 ruleset) every encoded line, including the trailing '=' of a soft break, is at most 76 characters
findings.actual: first line is 70 'a' + '=00=00' + '=' = 77 characters; the soft break after the third-from-last octet is emitted without checking that the encoded octet fits
findings.evidence: strict mode 'implements the full ruleset' of RFC 1521, whose rule #5 limits encoded lines to 76 characters; the code defines SAFE_LENGTH=73 to guarantee this but the third-from-last octet handling (pos += 3 then soft break when pos > SAFE_LENGTH-2) overshoots it

review.title: Strict-mode QuotedPrintableCodec can emit encoded lines longer than 76 characters
review.reason: Strict mode is documented as implementing the full RFC 1521 ruleset, including rule #5 (lines of at most 76 characters including the trailing '='). Tracing the source: after 70 'a' and the first 0x00 at index 70, pos is 74. The third-from-last octet (0x00 at index 71) is then encoded unconditionally, giving pos 77, and the soft-break check `pos > SAFE_LENGTH-2` appends '=', so the line has 77 characters. The same overshoot is reachable in the main loop: `pos < SAFE_LENGTH` allows an encoded 3-byte write from pos 72, so a later encoded octet followed by '=' can reach 78. A fix is to break before writing an encoded octet that would not fit. A maintainer would likely accept that, though the severity is low because few callers use strict mode with binary input.
